title: Real adopter reference validation
outOfScope: Any write, push, pull request, merge, tag, release, or provider-configuration change in a reference project.
Claiming provider identity, branch-protection, review, audit, or release evidence from local clones.
Treating a controlled fixture or this template repository as a reference project.
Changing the reference projects' product source, dependency manifests, CI, signing material, or existing governance files.

riskAssessment.reason: The Work Item runs non-destructive lifecycle validation in isolated clones of three external reference projects and must preserve evidence boundaries.

reasons: Installer, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, scope-violation, and evidence-integrity behavior are high-impact governance boundaries.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized the Work Item lifecycle; implementation remains limited to isolated local clones with no reference-provider writes.

preReviewWarnings: Review that every Evidence Pack records immutable source revision, every unavailable native toolchain is not_run, and no local-clone fact becomes a provider claim.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A deterministic runner selects three public, non-template reference projects matching the service, mobile, and enterprise-monorepo categories and records repository URL, immutable revision, baseline state, and project classification in a separate Evidence Pack for each.

Each Evidence Pack executes and records new-install dry run, conflict review, Makefile conflict, existing-agent-file preservation, calibration, first Work Item, scope violation, test weakening, injection, finish, local PR/merge/close simulation, upgrade, upgrade conflict, rollback, disable, enable, uninstall, and reinstall phases; unavailable native toolchains are not_run with a reason and recovery condition.
The runner proves that the reference clone's baseline product paths are unchanged except for installer-owned governance paths, and emits an explainable before/after Git diff classification.

Focused tests prove source identity validation, phase completeness, unavailability handling, ownership-diff enforcement, and prevention of fixture/template/provider overclaims; documentation describes command use and evidence limitations.
guidelines: Keep source repositories read-only: use disposable clones and never push or alter provider configuration.
Evidence Packs must distinguish executed local facts, not_run native-toolchain phases, and unsupported provider facts.
Fail closed when immutable source identity, required phase coverage, or non-governance diff preservation cannot be proved.

intent.problem: Existing adopter evidence is controlled-fixture evidence and cannot demonstrate how AI Cockpit behaves against varied, real project structures without conflating local validation with provider assurance.
constraints: Use three non-template public reference projects in isolated disposable clones.
Do not write to source remotes, create external pull requests, change provider configuration, or claim provider-backed facts.
Preserve original product files and report unavailable native toolchains as not_run with recovery conditions.
Keep test execution deterministic by unit-testing the runner with local repositories; record actual reference execution separately.
intent.rationale: Structured, immutable Evidence Packs make adopter applicability inspectable while retaining the boundary between observable local execution and external-provider assurance.

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the mobile catalog entry and focused unavailability regression tests.

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the runner and focused ownership-diff regression tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: local reference evidence does not become a provider or enterprise assurance claim

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused output-boundary tests and the documentation capability projection checks.
